_why: CP-5.3 identifier resolution. A ref field declares its RESOLVER -- a statement about how two EXISTING tools relate, which is why it needs no other team to start. A REGISTRY ROW, not a chat-service constant (W1): written as a constant it would be the hardcoding the PO rejected. Gated on 5.3-pilot, which measured this resolver on the population that actually failed: ZERO_EXACT 0 in every stratum, 83.3% of contested pairs resolving to exactly one, and ambiguity REAL at 37.5% of contested calls -- which is why there is no 'pick the best' arm.

EntityRef._subject: 338 failed calls / 11 sessions sent a human name into an entity id field
EntityRef._match_note: tier=='exact' is a MATCH-QUALITY signal, not a fuzzy score: the selector sets it when lower(cached_name) equals the query OR one of the entity's aliases does. It also normalises -- the model sent 'Lam Uyen' with different diacritics from the stored name and search still returned tier=exact.

_bindings_note: Bound where the resolver can actually be applied: a glossary tool whose schema ALSO carries book_id, because an entity name is only unique within its book. 9 other catalogue params named entity_id are deliberately NOT bound -- composition/kg/world/lore tools are scoped differently and a book-scoped resolver would be wrong there. That residue is stated, and test_THE_UNBOUND_ENTITY_REF_PARAMS_ARE_STATED keeps it visible instead of letting it look like coverage.
